newsitem.title: USA: Condensate output affecting oil markets - analyst.
newsitem.headline: Condensate output affecting oil markets - analyst.

text.p: Mounting condensate output in the coming years due to increased natural gas exploration, will create a new stream of feedstocks that might hurt refiner profits, an analyst told refiners Monday.

"Over time, a traded and liquid market in condensates could emerge," Kevin Lindemer, an analyst at Boston-based consultancy Cambridge Energy Research Associates, told executives attending the National Petroleum Refiners Association annual meeting.
Condensates are the heavier portion of natural gas deposits that tend to solidfy into liquids, and can be used as refinery feedstocks to make distillates or gasoline.
"In our view, going forward, condensates will be a major factor in keeping the gasoline market long (well supplied)," Lindemer said, noting 1996 marked the first year the trend was clarly in place.
Lindemer said that between now and the year 2010, condensates will grow to about eight percent of total liquids compared to no more than four percent currently.

Later, he told Reuters that means condensates now make up about 3 million barrels per day (bpd) of the world's total liquid demand of 70 million bpd, and that nummber will swell in just over a decade to about 7.5 million bpd of projected world liquids demand in 2010 of about 94 million bpd.
"Will these molecules find a home? We don't know how it's going to clear," he said. "There are a lot of different things that could happen," Lindemer said.

He said that while the growing volumes of condensate might contribute to a weak gasoline market, it might also spare some refiners the heavy investments required to process cheaper heavy crudes into pricey light products since condensate is already such a light feedstock in its natural state.
He also said the extra condensate could spur on technological development in the refining sector aimed at making "little molecules into big molecules."
-- Oliver Ludwig, New York Energy Desk 1 212 859 1620
